pr_title: Set IsRequired on ApiDescriptions for endpoints
pr_body:
- Use the same logic we have in RequestDelegateFactory.Create to
determine if a method parameter is required or not. We then set the
IsRequired property on the ApiParameterDesciption.
- Added tests

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/35081

~TODO: Figure out why tests don't properly expose NRT metadata. It might be because of this bug https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/55254~

issue_context.title: Set required parameter attribute in OpenAPI metadata
issue_context.body:
By default, OpenAPI assumes that all parameters are optional parameters.

https://swagger.io/docs/specification/describing-parameters/

We don't currently propagate any information that says `required: true` for parameters that are required in an endpoint

This builds on top of the work done in #32375
comments:
Turns out this requires changes in 2 places:
- We need to set the IsRequired flag on API explorer metadata
- We need to make sure consumers use this flag. Today Swashbuckle ignores this flag and determines optionality using custom logic (https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/pull/2183)

review_comments:
I looked at this because I know we have a similar `RequestDelegateFactoryTest` that passes. Specifically [RequestDelegateHandlesBodyParamOptionality](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/fa9dd9c5fe476706e33819ded8b96bf72a5fef41/src/Http/Http.Extensions/test/RequestDelegateFactoryTests.cs#L1565). At first, I thought it was just because that test used a local function rather than a lambda, so I was going to suggest switching to that for now until https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/55254 is fixed. It turns out switching to a local function didn't fix the test though.

Guess what *does* fix this test!!!

```suggestion
        }
                
        [Theory]
        [InlineData(null)]
        public void RandomTheory(object ignore)
        {
        }
```

I don't entirely know why. It doesn't really change anything about the IL generated for the `TestIsRequiredFromBody` test this somehow fixes.

What I did notice is adding this same `RandomTheory` method outside of the `#nullable enable` section *does not* fix this even though the theory doesn't mark anything as nullable.

Moving the `RandomTheory` into the nullable section does change the IL for `RandomTheory` by adding the `NullableContextAttribute` to the method, but I don't know why this affects the `TestIsRequiredFromBody` which doesn't have the attribute before or after the fix.

Is this at all related to https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/32804?

We have it enabled in aspnetcore repo to reduce DLL size. However, it probably only needs to be on for assemblies that we ship and not test assemblies.

I don't think so. This PR removed `nullablePublicOnly` from the `Features` property in the test project. https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/35233/files#diff-b73478a77d203a214533c8257af02a208e1d529c629f682f2e2c2999cac0da05R6
